title: session-load splits a capture's file reads by kind and counts no device as a path
goal: python3 _tools/benchmarks.py run session-load --fs-usage FILE writes per class, beside file_reads, the rows opens_read (open lines with R first in the mode), descriptor_reads (read, readv, pread, preadv) and disk_reads (RdData), since one read of one file can show as all three; and a RdData line with a device and no file path adds nothing to distinct_paths

run:
import sys
def _fail(t, e, tb, _d=sys.excepthook):
    if issubclass(t, AssertionError):
        print('check failed:', e); sys.exit(1)
    _d(t, e, tb)
sys.excepthook = _fail
import csv, os, shutil, subprocess, tempfile
T = tempfile.mkdtemp()
cap = os.path.join(T, 'fs_usage.txt')
L = [
    '13:21:46.312411  open              F=3        (R_____N____)  /work/kb/_tools/kbcommon.py                 0.000030   python3.4101',
    '13:21:46.312499  read              F=3    B=0x1a2b                                                       0.000011   python3.4101',
    '13:21:46.314000  RdData[A]         D=0x0012a3b0  B=0x1000   /dev/disk3s1                                0.000150 W python3.4101',
]
open(cap, 'w').write('\n'.join(L) + '\n')
out = os.path.join(T, 'out.csv')
p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '_tools/benchmarks.py', 'run', 'session-load', '--fs-usage', cap, '--out', out],
                   capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(out, encoding='utf-8'))) if os.path.exists(out) else []
shutil.rmtree(T, ignore_errors=True)
assert p.returncode == 0, ('run session-load --fs-usage exit', p.returncode, p.stderr[-400:])
val = {(r['case'], r['metric']): float(r['value']) for r in rows if r['scenario'] == 'session-load'}
for m in ('opens_read', 'descriptor_reads', 'disk_reads'):
    assert val.get(('capture kb-tools', m)) == 1, ('no split row of 1', m, val.get(('capture kb-tools', m)))
assert val.get(('capture kb-tools', 'distinct_paths')) == 1, ('a device counted as a path', val.get(('capture kb-tools', 'distinct_paths')))

Knowledge (researched in ST-x7npr7es): kb/public/python/macos-fs-usage-output.md lines 58-65 say a RdData/RdMeta/PgIn line prints D=, B= and /dev/<disk> before an optionally empty pathname, an errored disk I/O prints D= and [errno] with no /dev token, and CoreStorage lines print no path; a distinct_paths counter skips the /dev token.
